name: Asylum / Refugee Status and Subsidiary Protection

qualifying_event.description: A person with a well-founded fear of persecution (race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or social group membership) or facing real risk of serious harm may apply for refugee status or subsidiary protection.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Oral or written application at a border crossing, police station, or migration authority; identity information and reasons for seeking protection.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a well-founded fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership of a particular social group (Article 18).
Available to those not qualifying as refugees but facing a real risk of serious harm, including death penalty, torture, or threats arising from armed conflict (Article 20).

evidence_required.document: Written asylum application with identity information and grounds for protection
Supporting evidence of persecution or risk of serious harm

outcome.duration_length: Standard decision timeline 6 months, extendable up to 3 months for complex cases; maximum 21 months overall (Article 28)

sources.title: Republic of Albania -- Law No. 10/2021 on Asylum, official English translation hosted by the Ministry of Interior: refugee status (Art. 18), subsidiary protection (Art. 20), application process (Art. 26-27), work rights after 9 months if undecided (Art. 61), reception/housing (Art. 43), decision timeline (Art. 28)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Albania). Unusually well-documented for a humanitarian route in this dataset: the primary Asylum Law is hosted directly by the Ministry of Interior in English translation, with granular procedural detail (registration within 3-10 working days, free legal aid, pre-university education for minor applicants within 3 months, work rights kicking in automatically at the 9-month mark if no decision has issued). work_rights modeled 'restricted' to reflect this 9-month conditional trigger rather than 'none' or 'full' -- during the first 9 months (or until a decision, if earlier), applicants generally cannot work. pr_after_months/citizenship_after_months left null: the law confirms recognized refugees can eventually access family reunification (see al_family_reunification.json, which notes a 3-month expedited process for refugee family members) and, in principle, the general naturalization/permanent-residence tracks, but no refugee-specific accelerated timeline to PR or citizenship was found stated in this pass. Decision-making body: 'Authority responsible for asylum and refugees' at the relevant ministry, with the National Commission on Asylum and Refugees handling appeals and further recourse to administrative courts.
